newsitem.title: CHINA: China region in call to battle unrest, religion.
newsitem.headline: China region in call to battle unrest, religion.

text.p: China's restive northwestern region of Xinjiang has issued a new year's call to battle unrest and underground religious activities, the Xinjiang Daily said in an edition seen in Beijing on Saturday.

Xinjiang needed to study President Jiang Zemin's call to oppose separatist activities and should fight to preserve ethnic unity in the mostly Moslem region, the newspaper quoted Yusufu Aisha, vice-chairman of the Xinjiang regional government, as saying in its February 2 edition.

"In this new year... we must take a clear cut stand in carrying out the resolute struggle against ethnic splittism and illegal religious activities," Aisha was quoted as telling a symposium of regional officials in January.
Authorities must "protect national unity, protect ethnic unity and protect the stability of Xinjiang," Aisha said but gave no details as to how this should be done.
Xinjiang authorities last year stepped up a crackdown on separatists and unauthorised religious activity after a series of violent clashes, bombings and politically motivated assassination attempts.
